scenarioPaths.narrative: Support receives a customer-safe request, classifies it, links proof, updates the customer, and closes on approved docs.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: customer receives approved support wording and a docs source without raw evidence exposure

scenarioPaths.narrative: Security-sensitive evidence blocks customer-visible update until the security/legal owner route accepts it.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: request remains owner-routed with scope-out label instead of leaking customer data

scenarioPaths.narrative: A stale quickstart or proof fixture creates a customer-safe limitation update instead of an unsupported claim.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: support states limitation and next update condition before promising readiness

scenarioPaths.narrative: Incident-adjacent severity routes to incident communications while support preserves redacted context.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: incident commander receives context and support keeps customer-safe boundary wording

accessibilityNotes: Keyboard order follows intake, triage, evidence, owner route, customer update, then closure regions.
Screen reader labels include state, severity, owner route, redaction state, proof mode, and next update condition.
Contrast is not the only signal; blocked, stale, internal-only, and scope-out states include explicit text labels.
Motion is optional; status changes and timeline transitions must respect reduced-motion preferences.
scopeOut: No helpdesk software or ticket queue automation.
No customer-data access, secret access, or support impersonation.
No incident command, on-call staffing, runbook execution, or notification dispatch.
No contractual SLA promise, public response-time guarantee, or paid support term.
